paper.title: Admissibility of lagged single-source-of-error state space models: the per-lag eigenvalue check, the cancelled ARIMA form, the step-down test and their implementation in smooth

definitions.definition: A pure additive single-source-of-error state space model $y_t = w' v_{t-l} + \epsilon_t$, $v_t = F v_{t-l} + g \epsilon_t$ with $k$ components, in which component $j$ of $v_{t-l}$ enters with its own lag $l_j$; its discount matrix is $D = F - g w'$ and its lag matrix is $L(B) = \mathrm{diag}(B^{l_1}, \dots, B^{l_k})$ for the backshift operator $B$; $\Lambda(\lambda) = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda^{l_1}, \dots, \lambda^{l_k})$ for a complex number $\lambda$.

The transition matrix $\tilde D$ of size $\sum_j l_j$ of the lag-1 system equivalent to $v_t = D v_{t-l}$, in which component $j$ carries itself and its $l_j - 1$ lagged copies; $\tilde F$, $\tilde g$ and $\tilde w$ are expanded in the same way, so that $\tilde D = \tilde F - \tilde g \tilde w'$.

A lagged SSOE model has decaying weights when the weights $\tilde w' \tilde D^j \tilde g$ of the past observations in its fitted values tend to zero, that is, when every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of its expanded discount matrix that is reachable from $\tilde g$ and observable through $\tilde w$ has $|\lambda| < 1$; the largest such $|\lambda|$ is its largest mode modulus. A mode that $\tilde g$ does not reach but $\tilde w$ sees carries an initial state whose effect is not covered: with $|\lambda| > 1$ it grows.

The test applied by smoothEigens() of smooth 4.6.0 and of its repository until commit 4a44c1c (src/headers/eigenCalc.h) to models without adaptive regressors: every eigenvalue of every diagonal block of $D$, one block per unique lag, has modulus below 1; reimplemented in numpy as per_lag_max().

The largest modulus among the eigenvalues $\lambda$ of the expanded discount matrix for which the smallest singular values of $[\lambda I - \tilde D;\ \tilde w']$ and of $[\lambda I - \tilde D,\ \tilde g]$ both exceed $10^{-7}(\|\tilde D\|_2 + \|\tilde g\| + \|\tilde w\|)$ (Popov-Belevitch-Hautus rank tests), computed with numpy as pbh_max().

The procedure that computes the coefficients of $\theta(B) = \det(I - D L(B))$ and $\phi(B) = \det(I - F L(B))$ by an inverse discrete Fourier transform of their values at the $N$-th roots of unity ($N$ the smallest power of 2 above $\sum_j l_j$), and divides both by every cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_n(B)$, $n$ dividing one of the lags, for as long as it divides both with a remainder at most $10^{-9}$ times the sum of absolute coefficients; the quotient of $\theta$ is the cancelled MA polynomial $\theta^*(B)$.

The Levinson-Durbin step-down (Schur-Cohn) recursion on $1 + c_1 B + \dots + c_n B^n$: for $j = n, \dots, 1$, $\kappa_j = c_j$ and $c_i \leftarrow (c_i - \kappa_j c_{j-i}) / (1 - \kappa_j^2)$; the test passes when every $|\kappa_j| < 1$, which holds if and only if all roots lie outside the unit circle (the $\kappa_j$ are the partial autocorrelations of the autoregression with this polynomial).
Generalised Univariate Model of the smooth package: a lagged SSOE model whose $F$, $g$ and $w$ are all estimated.

Exponential smoothing with additive error, no trend and additive seasonality of period $m$; here in the lagged form with a level of lag 1 and one seasonal state of lag $m$, $F = I$, $w = (1, 1)'$, $g = (\alpha, \gamma)'$.

claims.statement: If the discount matrix $D$ of a [[D1:lagged SSOE model]] is block-diagonal with one block $D_{ll}$ per unique lag $l$, every eigenvalue of the [[D2:expanded discount matrix]] has modulus $|\mu|^{1/l}$ for an eigenvalue $\mu$ of some $D_{ll}$, so all of them lie inside the unit circle exactly when the [[D4:per-lag check]] passes.

scope.population: lagged SSOE models whose discount matrix is block-diagonal across lags

checks.notes: Re-derived by a Schur complement; 50 random block-diagonal D with lags from {1, 3, 4} gave moduli |mu|^(1/l) and agreeing decisions. Noted that the RN2 example labelled block-diagonal is lower-triangular, and that the claim does not cover ETS or GUM, whose D is not block-diagonal.
E7.S1 now rests on C15 for a general M; S2 needs the components grouped by lag, which a simultaneous permutation allows; the claim does not cover ETS or GUM, whose D is not block-diagonal.

claims.statement: An eigenvalue $\lambda \neq 0$ of the expanded transition matrix $\tilde F$ with an eigenvector unobservable through $\tilde w$ or a left eigenvector unreachable from $\tilde g$ is an eigenvalue of the [[D2:expanded discount matrix]], and $1/\lambda$ is a common root of $\phi(B) = \det(I - F L(B))$ and $\theta(B) = \det(I - D L(B))$.

checks.notes: Steps re-derived and checked on 5 random GUMs with a constructed unobservable mode (residuals about 1e-14). Noted that step S3 rested on the general identity of the expansion rather than on C7; the dependency now points to C15.

claims.statement: The numpy function per_lag_max() returns the same largest eigenvalue modulus as smoothEigensCpp() of smooth 4.6.0 (replaced in commit 4a44c1c) for models with a constant measurement vector and without adaptive regressors.

The [[D5:PBH reference]] with relative rank tolerance 1e-7 classifies every eigenvalue of modulus at least 1 of the [[D2:expanded discount matrix]] of the tested models correctly as both reachable and observable or not.

For the lag-1 expansion $\tilde M$ of $v_t = M v_{t-l}$ in a [[D1:lagged SSOE model]], $\det(\lambda I - \tilde M) = \det(\Lambda(\lambda) - M)$, which equals $\lambda^{\sum_j l_j} \det(I - M L(1/\lambda))$ for $\lambda \neq 0$.

conditions: any square matrix $M$ of size $k$

claims.statement: For a [[D1:lagged SSOE model]] with $\theta(B) = \det(I - D L(B))$ and $\phi(B) = \det(I - F L(B))$, the roots of $\theta(B) / \gcd(\theta(B), \phi(B))$ are exactly the reciprocals $1/\lambda$ of the nonzero eigenvalues $\lambda$ of the reachable and observable part of the [[D2:expanded discount matrix]] (its Kalman decomposition), with their multiplicities.

claims.statement: For a polynomial $c$ with $c(0) \neq 0$ and $r > 0$, the [[D7:step-down test]] passes on $c(B/r)$ if and only if $1/|B| < r$ for every root $B$ of $c$.

checks.notes: The scaling is correct and the equivalence rests on D7 and B2; noted the missing division by c(0) and the citation of D7 for a substitution in E15, since corrected.

claims.statement: In additive ETS models, and in GUM models with an identity transition or with transition, persistence and measurement in general position, every factor shared by $\theta(B)$ and $\phi(B)$ with a root in $|B| \le 1$ is a product of cyclotomic polynomials $\Phi_n(B)$ with $n$ dividing a lag of the model.

For a square matrix $M$ of size $k$ and lags $l_1, \dots, l_k$, $\det(I - M L(B)) = \sum_{S \subseteq \{1, \dots, k\}} (-1)^{|S|} \det(M_{SS})\, B^{\sum_{j \in S} l_j}$, with $\det(M_{\emptyset\emptyset}) = 1$.

scope.population: square matrices and positive integer lags

checks.notes: Steps of E16 re-derived; against the determinant at random complex B the relative error was at most 3.0e-15 for real M (200 cases) and complex M (100 cases).

claims.statement: The per-lag discount matrices $D_{m_i} = F_{m_i} - g_{m_i} w_{m_i}'$ of Section 5.4 of the ADAM monograph have as nonzero eigenvalues those of the diagonal block of $D = F - g w'$ for the lag $m_i$ (the [[D4:per-lag check]]), and their sum is $D + \sum_{i \neq j} g_{m_i} w_{m_j}'$, which differs from $D$ whenever $g w'$ links components of distinct lags.

scope.population: pure additive lagged SSOE models with more than one distinct lag
conditions: F split by the columns, and g and w by the components, of each lag, as in Section 5.2 of the monograph, which writes g_{m_i} and w_{m_i} without defining their split; with g kept whole the first part holds and the sum equals D

checks.notes: 500 random models with lags in {1, 3, 12}: the nonzero eigenvalues of each D_{m_i} equal those of the diagonal block of D, and the sum equals D plus the cross terms, never D with distinct lags. Noted the missing step for 'differs from D', the 'distinct lags' wording and the monograph's undefined split of g, since added to the evidence and the scope.

claims.statement: For ETS(A,N,A) with $m = 12$, $\alpha = 1.2$ and $\gamma = 0.9$, the stability condition of Section 5.4 of the ADAM monograph holds (largest nonzero eigenvalue modulus of its per-lag discount matrices 0.2), while in the full discount recursion the effect of the initial states on the fitted values and the weight of a past observation both grow by 1.0164 per period, and the largest root modulus of the cancelled MA polynomial is 1.0165.

conditions: alpha = 1.2, gamma = 0.9
initial states set to one or one unit observation, 2400 periods

relations.note: The monograph states that the model is stable when all the nonzero eigenvalues of the per-lag discount matrices D_{m_i} are below one in absolute value, and forecastable when the effect of the initial states through each D_{m_i} tends to a constant (eq. 5.22).

assessments.rationale: An exploratory but deterministic counterexample, with the growth of the recursion and the root of the polynomial computed separately and agreeing; one parameter pair, chosen from the planned grid test of the per-lag check.

evidence.foundation: linear algebra over the field of rational functions in $B$
evidence.description: Derivation of the ARIMA form of a lagged SSOE model by the matrix determinant lemma.

steps.statement: \epsilon_t = y_t - w' v_{t-l} \Rightarrow v_t = D v_{t-l} + g y_t,\ D = F - g w'
v_{t-l} = L(B) v_t \Rightarrow (I - D L(B)) v_t = g y_t
\det(I - D L(B))|_{B=0} = 1 \Rightarrow I - D L(B) \text{ is invertible over rational functions}
\epsilon_t = \left(1 - w' L(B) (I - D L(B))^{-1} g\right) y_t
I - D L(B) - g\, w' L(B) = I - F L(B)
\det(I - F L(B)) = \det(I - D L(B))\left(1 - w' L(B)(I - D L(B))^{-1} g\right)
steps.rule: matrix determinant lemma $\det(A - g u') = \det(A)(1 - u' A^{-1} g)$

steps.statement: \det(I - D L(B))\, \epsilon_t = \det(I - F L(B))\, y_t

evidence.foundation: linear algebra over the complex numbers
evidence.description: Characteristic polynomial of the expanded matrix and its factorisation for a block-diagonal discount matrix.

steps.statement: \det(\lambda I - \tilde M) = \det(\Lambda(\lambda) - M) \text{ for the lag-1 expansion } \tilde M \text{ of } v_t = M v_{t-l}
D = \mathrm{blockdiag}(D_{ll}) \Rightarrow \det(\Lambda(\lambda) - D) = \prod_l \det(\lambda^l I - D_{ll})
\det(\lambda^l I - D_{ll}) = 0 \iff \lambda^l = \mu,\ \mu \in \mathrm{eig}(D_{ll}) \Rightarrow |\lambda| = |\mu|^{1/l}
|\lambda| < 1 \iff |\mu| < 1

evidence.foundation: linear algebra over the complex numbers
evidence.description: Unobservable or unreachable modes of the expanded transition matrix are modes of the expanded discount matrix and give common roots of the two ARIMA-form polynomials.

steps.statement: \tilde F u = \lambda u,\ \tilde w' u = 0 \Rightarrow \tilde D u = \tilde F u - \tilde g (\tilde w' u) = \lambda u
steps.rule: substitution of $\tilde D = \tilde F - \tilde g \tilde w'$

steps.statement: u' \tilde F = \lambda u',\ u' \tilde g = 0 \Rightarrow u' \tilde D = u' \tilde F - (u' \tilde g) \tilde w' = \lambda u'
steps.rule: substitution of $\tilde D = \tilde F - \tilde g \tilde w'$

steps.statement: \det(\lambda I - \tilde M) = \lambda^{\sum_j l_j} \det(I - M L(1/\lambda)),\ \lambda \neq 0
\phi(1/\lambda) = \det(I - F L(1/\lambda)) = 0,\ \theta(1/\lambda) = \det(I - D L(1/\lambda)) = 0

evidence.description: Evaluation of the ARIMA-form polynomials of ETS(A,N,A) at $B = 1$.

steps.statement: D = \begin{pmatrix} 1-\alpha & -\alpha \\ -\gamma & 1-\gamma \end{pmatrix},\ L(B) = \mathrm{diag}(B, B^m)
\theta(B) = \det(I - D L(B)) = (1 - (1-\alpha)B)(1 - (1-\gamma)B^m) - \alpha\gamma B^{m+1}
\theta(1) = \alpha\gamma - \alpha\gamma = 0
\det(I - \tilde D) = 1^{m+1} \theta(1) = 0
steps.rule: identity of the lag-1 expansion at $\lambda = 1$

evidence.foundation: linear algebra over the complex numbers
evidence.description: Schur-complement derivation of the characteristic polynomial of the lag-1 expansion.

steps.statement: \lambda I - \tilde M = \begin{pmatrix} \lambda I_k - A & -B \\ -C & \lambda I - S \end{pmatrix}
steps.rule: partition of the states into the $k$ current values (heads) and the $\sum_j (l_j - 1)$ lagged copies (tails); $S$ shifts each tail chain, $C$ feeds each head into its first copy, $A$ and $B$ hold the entries of $M$ that act on heads with lag 1 and on last copies

steps.statement: \det(\lambda I - S) = \lambda^{\sum_j (l_j - 1)}
steps.rule: determinant of a lower-triangular matrix with diagonal $\lambda$

steps.statement: A + B (\lambda I - S)^{-1} C = M\, \mathrm{diag}(\lambda^{1 - l_1}, \dots, \lambda^{1 - l_k}),\ \lambda \neq 0
steps.rule: $(\lambda I - S)^{-1} C$ maps head $j$ to its copies $\lambda^{-s}$, $s = 1, \dots, l_j - 1$, and $B$ reads copy $l_i - 1$ of component $i$

steps.statement: \det(\lambda I - \tilde M) = \lambda^{\sum_j (l_j - 1)} \det(\lambda I_k - M\, \mathrm{diag}(\lambda^{1 - l_j})) = \det(\Lambda(\lambda) - M),\ \lambda \neq 0
steps.rule: Schur complement, then factoring $\lambda\, \Lambda(\lambda)^{-1}$ out on the right

steps.statement: \det(\lambda I - \tilde M) = \det(\Lambda(\lambda) - M) \text{ for all } \lambda
steps.rule: two polynomials equal on $\lambda \neq 0$ are equal

steps.statement: \det(\lambda I - \tilde M) = \lambda^{\sum_j l_j} \det(I - M L(1/\lambda)),\ \lambda \neq 0
steps.rule: factoring $\Lambda(\lambda)$ out on the right: $\Lambda(\lambda) - M = (I - M \Lambda(\lambda)^{-1}) \Lambda(\lambda)$

evidence.foundation: linear systems theory over the complex numbers
evidence.description: The reduced form of the ARIMA polynomials through the Kalman decomposition of the expanded system.

steps.statement: \exists T: T^{-1}\tilde F T \text{ block-triangular with a reachable and observable block } (F_{co}, g_{co}, w_{co}),\ \tilde w'(zI - \tilde F)^{-1}\tilde g = w_{co}'(zI - F_{co})^{-1} g_{co}
\tilde D = \tilde F - \tilde g \tilde w' \text{ keeps the reachable and the unobservable subspaces, so } D_{co} = F_{co} - g_{co} w_{co}'
steps.rule: reachability is invariant under state feedback and observability under output injection

steps.statement: 1 + w_{co}'(zI - F_{co})^{-1} g_{co} = \frac{\det(zI - D_{co})}{\det(zI - F_{co})},\ \gcd(\det(zI - D_{co}), \det(zI - F_{co})) = 1
steps.rule: matrix determinant lemma; a single-input single-output realisation is minimal if and only if the numerator and denominator of its transfer function are coprime

steps.statement: 1 + \tilde w'(zI - \tilde F)^{-1}\tilde g = \frac{\det(zI - \tilde D)}{\det(zI - \tilde F)} = \frac{\theta(1/z)}{\phi(1/z)}
steps.rule: matrix determinant lemma and the identity of the lag-1 expansion

steps.statement: \frac{\theta(B)}{\gcd(\theta, \phi)}(B) = 0 \iff B = 1/\lambda,\ \lambda \in \mathrm{spec}(D_{co}) \setminus \{0\} \text{ (with multiplicity)}
steps.rule: uniqueness of the reduced fraction, with z = 1/B: the eigenvalues at zero give no root, theta(0) = phi(0) = 1 makes theta / gcd the reduced numerator, and the reversal keeps coprimality away from B = 0

evidence.description: Scaling the argument of a polynomial scales its roots.

steps.statement: c(B_i) = 0 \iff c((r B_i) / r) = 0
|r B_i| > 1\ \forall i \iff 1/|B_i| < r\ \forall i
c(B/r) / c(0) = 1 + \sum_i (c_i / c_0)\, r^{-i} B^i \text{ has the roots of } c(B/r)
\text{the step-down passes on } c(B/r) \iff |r B_i| > 1\ \forall i
steps.rule: the step-down test passes exactly when all roots lie outside the unit circle

evidence.foundation: linear algebra over the field of rational functions in $B$
evidence.description: Expansion of det(I - M L(B)) by multilinearity in the columns.

steps.statement: \text{column } j \text{ of } I - M L(B) = e_j - B^{l_j} m_j
\det(I - M L(B)) = \sum_{S} \det\left[\, e_j\ (j \notin S),\ -B^{l_j} m_j\ (j \in S) \right]
steps.rule: multilinearity of the determinant in the columns

steps.statement: \det\left[\, e_j\ (j \notin S),\ -B^{l_j} m_j\ (j \in S) \right] = (-1)^{|S|} B^{\sum_{j \in S} l_j} \det(M_{SS})
steps.rule: Laplace expansion along the unit columns, and pulling the scalars out of the other columns

evidence.foundation: linear algebra over the complex numbers
evidence.description: The per-lag discount matrices of Section 5.4 of the ADAM monograph against D.

steps.statement: F_{m_i} = F_{\cdot S_i},\ g_{m_i} = g_{S_i},\ w_{m_i} = w_{S_i} \text{ (zero elsewhere), } S_i \text{ the components of lag } m_i
steps.rule: the split of Section 5.2 of the monograph

steps.statement: D_{m_i} = F_{m_i} - g_{m_i} w_{m_i}' \text{ has non-zero columns only in } S_i
D_{m_i} \sim \begin{pmatrix} D_{S_i S_i} & 0 \\ \ast & 0 \end{pmatrix} \Rightarrow \mathrm{spec}(D_{m_i}) \setminus \{0\} = \mathrm{spec}(D_{S_i S_i}) \setminus \{0\}
steps.rule: a symmetric permutation and the eigenvalues of a block-triangular matrix

steps.statement: \sum_i D_{m_i} = F - \sum_i g_{m_i} w_{m_i}' = D + \sum_{i \neq j} g_{m_i} w_{m_j}'
(a, b) \text{ with lags } m_i \neq m_j: \left(\sum_{i \neq j} g_{m_i} w_{m_j}'\right)_{ab} = g_a w_b
steps.rule: a single term, so the sum differs from D exactly where g w' links components of different lags

limitations.statement: The 3042 ETS(A,N,A) models of the planned test of the per-lag check form the same fixed grid as exploratory run RN3, whose result prompted the hypothesis; only the 200 GUM models of that test were new data.
The PBH reference and the cyclotomic cancellation were written by the same agent and share the lag-1 expansion code and numpy's LAPACK eigenvalue routines; no independent implementation was compared.

The random model sets (persistence ranges, the probabilities of zero persistence and of a constant, the standard deviations of the GUM matrices) were chosen by the agent and not drawn from models estimated on data.

The reference decisions use numpy's polynomial roots (companion-matrix eigenvalues) for polynomials of degree up to 535 before cancellation with many roots near the unit circle, whose accuracy there was not checked by a second method.

The plans of the tests behind the step-down and bisection claims stated MA polynomial degrees up to 366; the generator code named in the plans, run unchanged, produced degrees up to 535 before cancellation.
The recursion of the counterexample to the monograph's condition was run for one parameter pair, with the initial states set to one and no data.
The fit timings come from one machine, seven repeats per fit, with a run-to-run variation of about 10% between benchmark runs of the same code.

For GUM models with structured parameters, such as a state with |F_ii| > 1 and zero persistence, theta and phi can share a factor with a root in |B| <= 1 that is not cyclotomic; the check keeps it and rejects the model although its observation weights decay, because the initial state of that mode has a growing effect.
